frq.setsNote: Whole released free-response sets (PDF, College Board) for the current exam format, linked from the course's past-exam-questions page and checked to load on 2026-11-14. College Board released two sets for each of 2023–2025 and one for 2026. Each set has one Article Analysis Question and one Evidence-Based Question; they are not matched to units, because both question types draw on research methods and on content from across the course. Scoring guidelines are on the past-exam-questions page.

frameworkCheck.title: AP Psychology Course and Exam Description (effective Fall 2025)
frameworkCheck.how: The 35 numbered CED topics (1.1–5.5) and their essential knowledge statements and exclusion statements were read from the course framework in the current PDF on AP Central; each topic is matched to the StudySprint topic whose guide section and questions teach it, and the questions stay inside the CED's stated limits (for example, only the eight listed neurotransmitters, the five listed hormones, and the listed sleep disorders). The four science practices and their eleven skills were read from the CED's science practices table, and each question is tagged with the skill it mainly uses. The Clarifications and Corrections implemented as of October 2025 (https://apcentral.collegeboard.org/media/pdf/ap-psychology-course-and-exam-description-clarifications.pdf) were checked: they revise wording in topics 1.3, 1.4, 1.5, 3.7, and 3.8 (for example, the all-or-none principle, alertness as a reticular activating system function, and the description of spontaneous recovery), add a list of psychological perspectives to skill 1.A and effect-size guidance to skill 3.C, and change part D of the Article Analysis Question; the guides follow the corrected wording.
frameworkCheck.weightsSource: the AP Students course page and the CED's exam section (each unit 15%–25% of the exam), both checked 2026-11-14
frameworkCheck.examFormat: From the AP Students assessment page and the CED (2 hours 40 minutes, digital in Bluebook): Section I, 75 multiple-choice questions in 90 minutes (66.7% of the score), a mix of individual questions and question sets built on a stimulus; the CED gives approximate multiple-choice weights of 65% Concept Application, 25% Research Methods and Design, and 10% Data Interpretation (Argumentation is not assessed in multiple choice). Section II, 2 free-response questions in 70 minutes (33.3%): an Article Analysis Question (16.65%, 25 minutes including a 10-minute reading period) on one summarized peer-reviewed study, and an Evidence-Based Question (16.65%, 45 minutes including a 15-minute reading period) that asks for a claim supported with evidence from three summarized sources. StudySprint practice is multiple-choice only, with individual questions and question sets built on hypothetical study summaries and data; written-response practice uses College Board's released questions.

skills.text: Apply psychological perspectives, theories, concepts, and research findings to a scenario.
Explain how cultural norms, expectations, and circumstances, as well as cognitive biases apply to behavior and mental processes.
Determine the type of research design(s) used in a given study.
Evaluate the appropriate use of research design elements in experimental methodology.
Evaluate the appropriate use of research design elements in non-experimental methodologies.
Evaluate whether a psychological research scenario followed appropriate ethical procedures.
Identify psychology-related concepts in descriptions or representations of data.
Calculate and interpret measures of central tendency, variation, and percentile rank in a given data set.
Interpret quantitative or qualitative inferential data from a given table, graph, chart, figure, or diagram.
Provide reasoning that is grounded in scientifically derived evidence to support, refute, or modify an established or provided claim, policy, or norm.

differences: The AP Students page's unit topic lists are summaries. Its Unit 3 list names development topics only, while the CED's Unit 3 (Development and Learning) also includes topics 3.7–3.9 on classical conditioning, operant conditioning, and social, cognitive, and neurological factors in learning; StudySprint teaches those topics in Unit 3 and lists them as framework topics.
The CED's 35 topics are the required content and are listed per unit as framework topics.

In the current CED, five learning objectives have no essential knowledge statements printed under them (checked on the rendered PDF pages): 3.1.B (cross-sectional and longitudinal designs), 3.3.A (how sex and gender influence socialization), 4.1.B (locus of control), 5.1.A (how health psychology addresses physical health and wellness), and 5.5.E (how group therapy differs from individual therapy). StudySprint teaches these briefly from the objective wording and widely used introductory definitions; that coverage is unverified against any more detailed College Board statement.
StudySprint's study summaries and data are labelled hypothetical; the AP Exam's free-response questions use summaries of real peer-reviewed studies.
